summary: Backend-only verification of the vehicle QR scan-alert WhatsApp/SMS fan-out fix in public_qr_alert, plus regressions on tag alerts and core auth/public APIs. 13/13 pytest tests passed. CONFIRMED FIXED: anonymous POST /api/public/qr/{qr_id}/alert returns 200 {id,type,ok:true} and now triggers a WhatsApp send attempt for the owner AND opted-in vehicle contacts (mock mode in preview), audited in db.notifications with meta.kind=scan_alert. Verified for emergency, wrong_parking and theft types.

minor.issue: allow_origins=["*"] combined with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec (browsers reject credentialed wildcard). Low impact today since auth is Bearer-token, not cookies, but should use explicit origins from env.
No brute-force lockout (no failed_attempts/lock_until logic); only IP rate-limiting (10/min). Playbook expects lockout after 5 failed attempts.
seed_admin/seed_demo only insert when missing — an ADMIN_PASSWORD/DEMO_PASSWORD change in .env is never applied to an existing user (playbook expects password update on change).

Fan-out is awaited inline in the request path (loop of notify_whatsapp per contact). Fine in mock (<0.5s) but with live MSG91 + many contacts this adds latency; consider asyncio.create_task/background task.
Emergent Push returns 401 'invalid X-Push-Key' in preview (expected/mocked) — handled gracefully as a WARNING, no 5xx.

action_items: Optional hardening: replace CORS wildcard+credentials with explicit origins from env
Optional: add failed-login lockout and make admin/demo seed update password when env password changes
Optional: move the WhatsApp/SMS fan-out loop off the request path (background task) before enabling live MSG91 for many contacts
critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified correct: notify_whatsapp -> send_sms fallback triggers only when status == 'failed'; comms.send_whatsapp returns 'failed' on non-2xx/exception in live mode, so the SMS fallback will work on the VPS. In preview it returns 'mock', so no SMS fallback is logged for vehicle alerts — expected.

Fan-out loop is wrapped in try/except and runs after db.alerts.insert_one, so a missing/invalid phone cannot break the alert insert or return a 5xx (validated: 200 in <1s, 404 for unknown qr_id, 422 for invalid type).

Owner phone is prepended to channels and duplicate suppression is absent — if the owner is also stored as a vehicle contact they will receive two identical messages. Consider de-duplicating the phone list.
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted one TEST_contact (+919999000111) on the demo vehicle. Created 4 alerts on the existing demo vehicle (TSF714F3) via the public scan endpoint; no seeded data modified.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Vehicle alert fan-out verified via log offsets on /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log (grep '[MSG91 WHATSAPP MOCK]') and db.notifications (meta.kind=scan_alert). Login is IP rate-limited 10/min — reuse module-scoped token fixtures. Auth is Bearer-token only (no httpOnly cookie on login), so playbook cookie/lockout checks do not apply as written.
rca_of_the_issue: Previously public_qr_alert only stored contact_channels and fired a push, so no WhatsApp/SMS ever left the server for vehicle scans. The new loop over channels calling notify_whatsapp (with send_sms fallback) now executes — proven by fresh '[MSG91 WHATSAPP MOCK] to=+910000000001 :: EMERGENCY: Your vehicle TSF714F3 was reported via a Nek Sathi QR scan...' log lines and matching db.notifications docs. On the VPS the user must set MSG91_WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE (+AUTHKEY/NUMBER) and MSG91_SMS_FLOW_ID for live delivery; masked-call ringing needs VOBIZ_* config (out of scope).
